title: Maximal isometric axial rotation moment, standing (B200 Isostation), males

quantity.name: primary axial rotation moment at MVC
quantity.definition: mean torque over stable 3 s of a 5-s maximal isometric axial rotation

source.authors: Ng JK-F, Parnianpour M, Richardson CA, Kippers V
source.sample: healthy right-handed males without history of back pain

protocol.summary: Erect standing in a B200 Isostation triaxial dynamometer (mechanically locked in 3 planes), L5-S1 interspinous space aligned with the flexion/extension axis; pelvis and lower legs stabilised by pelvic restraint, thigh and knee straps; torso fixed by chest restraint and thoracic pad; arms folded across the chest above the chest restraint. MVCs (5 s, 2 min rest) in flexion, extension, right/left lateral flexion and right/left axial rotation with visual feedback; then submaximal right/left axial rotation at 70, 50, 30% MVC (visual target). Torques = mean over stable 3 s, baseline (relaxed standing in device) subtracted; moments measured about the dynamometer axes (flexion/extension axis at L5-S1 interspinous space).
how_to_simulate: Upright standing, pelvis and legs fixed, thorax restrained by chest pad (isometric)
Maximal voluntary axial rotation right and left
Compare predicted maximal axial moment at L5-S1 with mean ± SD
protocol.notes: Reference point: dynamometer axes, flexion/extension axis aligned with L5-S1 interspinous space. Right vs left not significantly different. Flexion/extension/lateral MVC values were measured but not reported numerically.

extraction.check_notes: Re-read from page image: 78.3±24.9 (right) and 77.6±18.6 Nm (left).
